item.title: Do you know signs of a stroke? BE FAST are the words to remember
item.description: Sen. Chris Murphy is expected to fully recover from his stroke. The acronym BE FAST can help you remember the symptoms of stroke and what to do when it happens: Call 911 quickly.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Chris Murphy is expected to fully recover from his stroke. The acronym BE FAST can help you remember the symptoms of stroke and what to do when it happens: Call 911 quickly.

(Image credit: Allison Robbert)

item.title: Haley Stevens endorses GOP candidate in Michigan Senate race, spurning Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: Rep. Haley Stevens was scheduled to attend a unity event today with Abdul El-Sayed, who beat her in the Democratic primary. Instead, she endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Haley Stevens was scheduled to attend a unity event today with Abdul El-Sayed, who beat her in the Democratic primary. Instead, she endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.

(Image credit: Jose Juarez)

item.title: Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy is hospitalized with a stroke
item.description: Murphy's office says he was taken to the hospital this weekend after experiencing numbness in his arm. His chief of staff said he is responding well to treatment and expected to make a full recovery.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Judge tosses Trump's attempt to block Alaska Senate results if GOP incumbent loses
item.description: A federal judge has dismissed a highly unusual lawsuit by the Trump administration that tried to block the certification of results from Alaska's U.S. Senate race if the Republican incumbent lost.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The midterms will test the nation's political direction and confidence
item.description: At least some portion of the nation is likely to have its political confidence — and perhaps even its sense of security — tested in the days and weeks ahead. That test could also continue for some time to come.

item.title: New York City Marathon: Sweden's Almgren and Kenya's Chepkirui win as 60,000 take part
item.description: Andreas Almgren of Sweden won the men's race of the New York City Marathon in his debut in the event while Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women's race on Sunday for the second time.
item.content:encoded:
